evidence.claim: Adding a Redis CacheManager does NOT create a duplicate-bean failure by itself: Spring Boot's CacheAutoConfiguration is annotated @ConditionalOnMissingBean(value=CacheManager.class, name="cacheResolver") at class level and @AutoConfiguration(after=RedisAutoConfiguration), so the existing CacheConfig.cacheManager bean suppresses all auto-configured cache managers. The break only happens if a node adds a *second* explicit CacheManager bean. Replacing the body of CacheConfig.cacheManager is therefore the safe move.
evidence.source: javap -v on org/springframework/boot/autoconfigure/cache/CacheAutoConfiguration.class extracted from ~/.m2/.../spring-boot-autoconfigure-3.5.16.jar — class-level RuntimeVisibleAnnotations show ConditionalOnClass(CacheManager), ConditionalOnBean(CacheAspectSupport), ConditionalOnMissingBean(value=[CacheManager], name=["cacheResolver"])

evidence.claim: The shipped cache TTL exceeds the takedown bound Q1 committed to: application.yml sets app.cache.spec: maximumSize=10000,expireAfterWrite=5m, and CacheConfig hard-codes the same 5m as its @Value default. Both have to move to <=60s, or a missed invalidation breaches AC9 by up to five minutes.

application.yml today carries datasource, JPA (ddl-auto: validate), Flyway, server, actuator exposure and app.cache.spec only — no Redis connection, no JWT key or TTL, no rate-limit buckets, no default expiry, no public base URL. Every one of those is configuration under A5/A7/A13/A15 and Q7/Q8, and only the implement node can write this file.

The test harness starts PostgreSQL only, in a static initialiser deliberately not managed by the @Testcontainers extension (the javadoc records a thirty-minute build caused by getting that wrong). Any Redis container must follow the same singleton pattern, and it is added by test-contract/author-tests, not by implement.

options.summary: Cache: replace the body of CacheConfig.cacheManager with a RedisCacheManager (keeping the method name and the LINKS_CACHE constant), rather than adding a second cache configuration class. Verified to be conflict-free because Boot's cache auto-config backs off entirely when one CacheManager bean exists.

Cache: two-tier — a small Caffeine near-cache in front of Redis, one bean marked @Primary. Buys a few hundred microseconds on the hottest link (AC22) but reintroduces a per-instance layer that active invalidation cannot reach, so the 60s bound would rest on the near-cache TTL as well.

Auth libraries: take spring-security-crypto (for the KDF) plus jjwt-api/impl/jackson with literal versions, and do NOT take spring-boot-starter-security. Session verification is a plain filter/interceptor, so nothing auto-secures the click path or actuator.

Auth libraries: take spring-boot-starter-security and configure a permitAll SecurityFilterChain for /{code} and /actuator. More idiomatic, but a single missing matcher 401s the public redirect path and breaks AC14, and the failure is a passing build with failing tests.

Rate limiting: hand-roll the token bucket as a Lua script evaluated through the RedisTemplate the Redis starter already provides. No extra dependency, no second supply-chain approval, and single-key operations stay Cluster-safe.

Rate limiting: add a third-party bucket library. Saves writing the script but adds an unmanaged, explicitly versioned artifact to the frozen pom (the bucket4j coordinate guessed here did not resolve at the version tried, so coordinates need verifying before freezing).

unknowns.current_best_answer: Single instance or Sentinel, AOF appendfsync everysec, noeviction — this is exactly what Q5's approved answer assumes. Design should keep every Redis operation single-key or hash-tagged so a later Cluster move is additive.
unknowns.how_to_settle: Ask whoever runs the shared Redis, or run `redis-cli INFO persistence`, `redis-cli CONFIG GET maxmemory-policy` and `redis-cli INFO replication` against the target instance. One sentence from the platform owner settles it.
unknowns.question: Is the in-house Redis a single instance/Sentinel with AOF persistence and no key eviction, or a Cluster and/or a cache-only deployment with maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru?
unknowns.why_it_matters: A9/Q5 make Redis the durable buffer for click counts and A13 keys rate limits there. Under allkeys-lru a counter key can be silently evicted before flush, which loses clicks against AC3 with no error anywhere. Cluster mode additionally forbids multi-key Lua without hash tags and changes the Spring connection config, so getting it wrong is a rewrite of the counter and rate-limit code, not an edit.

It also decides whether application.yml carries key material at all.
